text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000150 bills 99215 far above its risk-adjusted expectation, and most of those visits are on patients with few or no chronic conditions, but the documentation sample is too small to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern itself is concerning. The excess 99215 share holds at every complexity tier, and over half of the 99215s fall on patients with zero or one chronic condition. The sampled low-complexity 99215s include routine presentations such as unspecified abdominal pain (C0065981, C0066347), UTI (C0065993, C0066250), rash (C0066101) and an upper respiratory infection (C0066344), which would not usually support high-complexity decision-making. Against that, the few charts that came back all supported the billed level, including the three documented 99215s with high MDM (C0066360, C0066386, C0066388). No data-review inflation was seen on claims without lab or test lines. With only 3 documented 99215s, the records are too thin to judge either way. The reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the zero-condition acute-complaint visits listed above, and check whether their MDM and time genuinely support level 5 or show cloned or templated notes."}
